findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: google_checkout_readiness, can_agent_checkout, check_agent_readiness, get_fixes, bulk_create_monitors · Private data: report_checkout, bulk_create_monitors · Public sink: report_checkout, ask_agents_about_brand · Destructive: get_readiness_result, bulk_create_monitors, list_monitors, monitor_summary, run_monitor_now.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: google_checkout_readiness, can_agent_checkout, check_agent_readiness, get_fixes, bulk_create_monitors · Private data: report_checkout, bulk_create_monitors · Public sink: report_checkout, ask_agents_about_brand · Destructive: get_readiness_result, bulk_create_monitors, list_monitors, monitor_summary, run_monitor_now

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

title: Tool description changed since last scan
detail: Tool "report_checkout" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Report how far one agent got at one store. Free, no login. Omit contributor_key and ARC issues one. Emails, phones, street addresses, and card numbers are rejected. The report stays private until 3 independent contributors agree within 14 days. Same as POST /api/outcomes." → after: "Report how far one agent got at one store. Free, no login. Omit contributor_key and ARC issues one. Emails, phones, street addresses, card numbers, IP addresses, and private hosts are rejected. The report stays private until 3 independent contributors with a day-old key, or enough reputation, agree "

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
